author: agent
question: Can an AI agent use my computer for me without guessing from screenshots?

points.claim: agent-desktop reads apps through the OS accessibility tree, not pixel matching.
points.spoken: It reads your apps through the accessibility tree, the same structure screen readers use.
points.source_note: README intro: 'through the OS accessibility tree... with no pixel matching'

visual.intent: three-step loop as the README gives it

points.title: Read the UI, not pixels
points.sub: Every snapshot lists the elements the agent can act on.

points.claim: Each actionable element gets a ref, so the agent acts on a target, not a guess.
points.spoken: Every element gets a ref, so the agent clicks a target instead of a guessed spot.
points.source_note: README quick start: 'a snapshot returns JSON with a ref for every element'

visual.intent: the three platforms the README's support table lists

points.title: A ref for every element
points.sub: The same loop runs on macOS, Windows and Linux.

points.claim: When the UI changes, a stale ref fails safely and the agent must snapshot again.
points.spoken: If the screen changes, the old reference fails safely, and the agent takes a fresh snapshot.
points.source_note: README: 'When the UI changes, an action returns STALE_REF... take a new snapshot'

visual.intent: failure path: act, stale ref, new snapshot, retry

points.title: Stale refs fail safely
points.sub: A changed screen returns an error, not a wrong click.

points.claim: It installs with one npm command and is open source.
points.spoken: Install it with one npm command. The source is open for anyone to read.
points.source_note: README installation: 'npm install -g agent-desktop'; repo is open source

visual.intent: install command, then the version check, as the README shows

points.title: One command to install
points.sub: Install with npm, then check the version.

catch: On macOS, you grant Accessibility permission first.
catch_sub: The README walks you through the Accessibility grant.

catch_visual.intent: permission step before any command runs

cover.visual: designed graphic: an accessibility-tree window with refs

media.design: Full-bleed window of a desktop app drawn as its accessibility tree: each row shows a ref id such as @s8f3k2p9:e8, the acting element is highlighted.
A framed desktop window with the snapshot JSON panel beside it, showing a ref for each button; the cursor lands on one ref, not a pixel guess.
Split layout: top shows a ref that failed with STALE_REF, bottom shows the fresh snapshot with a new ref id and the retry.

cta: Would you let an agent use your desktop? Comment DESKTOP and I'll pin the repo link.

youtube.title: agent-desktop: Let AI Use Your Desktop Apps
youtube.description:
agent-desktop lets an AI agent read and operate desktop apps through the OS accessibility tree. Each element gets a ref, so the agent acts on a target instead of a pixel guess. Open source, installs with npm.
Repo: https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-desktop
